subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 2(v) - Residential Status under FEMA
question: Mr. Rohan, an Indian citizen, resided in India for 210 days during FY 2022-23. On May 10, 2023, he went to London to take up an employment contract for a duration of 3 years. What is Mr. Rohan's residential status under Section 2(v) of FEMA, 1999 for FY 2023-24?
options: Person Resident Outside India (PROI) with effect from May 10, 2023, because he went outside India for taking up employment outside India.
Person Resident in India (PRII) for the entire FY 2023-24 because his stay in India in FY 2022-23 exceeded 182 days.
Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident as defined under the Income-tax Act, 1961.
Dual resident entitled to relief under double tax avoidance agreements.
ref: Section 2(v)(i)(A) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
explanation: Under Section 2(v)(i), 'person resident in India' means a person residing in India for more than 182 days during the course of the preceding financial year, but DOES NOT INCLUDE a person who has gone out of India or who stays outside India for or on taking up employment outside India (Clause A). Since Rohan went abroad for employment, he becomes a Person Resident Outside India (PROI) from the date of departure.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 5 & FEM (CAT) Rules - Prohibited Current Account Transactions
question: Under the Foreign Exchange Management (Current Account Transactions) Rules, 2000, which of the following current account transactions is completely PROHIBITED under Schedule I?
options: Remittance out of lottery winnings, racing/riding income, purchase of lottery tickets, football pools, and sweepstakes.
Remittance for cultural tours.
Remittance for hiring transponders for TV channels.
Remittance of commission on exports under Rupee State Credit Route.
ref: Schedule I of FEM (Current Account Transactions) Rules, 2000 read with Section 5
explanation: Under Schedule I of FEM (Current Account Transactions) Rules, 2000, remittance out of lottery winnings, remittance of income from racing/riding or any other hobby, remittance for purchase of lottery tickets, banned/proscribed magazines, football pools, sweepstakes, etc., are completely prohibited.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Schedule III & LRS - Liberalised Remittance Scheme Ceiling
question: Mr. Kapoor, an individual resident in India, intends to remit foreign exchange abroad for his son's overseas education and his family holiday. Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) of RBI read with Schedule III of FEM (CAT) Rules, what is the annual permissible ceiling for all permissible current and capital account transactions per financial year?
options: Up to USD 2,50,000 (Two Hundred Fifty Thousand US Dollars) or its equivalent per financial year (April-March) without prior RBI approval.
Up to USD 1,00,000 per financial year.
Up to USD 5,00,000 per calendar year.
Unlimited remittances provided TCS at 20% is collected.
ref: Schedule III of FEM (CAT) Rules, 2000 read with RBI A.P. (DIR Series) Circulars on LRS
explanation: Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), resident individuals are freely permitted to remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year (April-March) for any permissible current or capital account transactions or a combination of both without prior approval of RBI. Any remittance exceeding USD 2,50,000 requires prior approval of the Reserve Bank.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 6 - Permissible Capital Account Transactions
question: Which of the following is explicitly classified as a 'Capital Account Transaction' under Section 2(e) read with Section 6 of FEMA, 1999?
options: Investment in foreign securities by a resident Indian, raising of foreign currency loans (ECBs), and transfer of immovable property outside India by a person resident in India.
Payment due as interest on loans and as net income from investments.
Remittance for living expenses of parents residing abroad.
Payment due in connection with foreign trade and short-term banking credit facilities.
ref: Section 2(e) and Section 6(3) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
explanation: Under Section 2(e), 'capital account transaction' means a transaction which alters the assets or liabilities, including contingent liabilities, outside India of persons resident in India or assets or liabilities in India of persons resident outside India. Foreign security investments, foreign loans (ECBs), and overseas immovable property transfers alter such balance sheets and are capital account transactions.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] FDI Policy - Prohibited Sectors for Foreign Direct Investment
question: Under the Consolidated Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Policy and Non-Debt Instruments (NDI) Rules, 2019, in which of the following sectors is Foreign Direct Investment completely PROHIBITED?
options: Lottery business, gambling and betting, chit funds, Nidhi company, trading in Transferable Development Rights (TDRs), Real Estate Business or construction of farm houses, manufacturing of cigars, cheroots, cigarillos and cigarettes of tobacco.
Single-brand product retail trading.
Civil aviation and non-scheduled air transport services.
Pharmaceuticals (Greenfield manufacturing).
ref: Rule 15 read with Schedule I of FEM (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019
explanation: FDI is strictly prohibited in: (a) Lottery business including government/private lottery, online lotteries; (b) Gambling and betting including casinos; (c) Chit funds; (d) Nidhi company; (e) Trading in TDRs; (f) Real Estate Business (excluding township/construction development); (g) Manufacturing of cigars/cigarettes; (h) Sectors not open to private investment (Atomic energy & Railway operations).

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Land Border FDI Restrictions (Press Note 3 / Rule 6 Proviso)
question: Under the proviso to Rule 6 of the FEM (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019 (reflecting Press Note 3 of 2020), an entity of a country which shares a land border with India can invest in Indian companies only under which route?
options: Only under the Government Approval Route, regardless of the sector or percentage of foreign holding.
Under 100% Automatic Route provided it is in technology manufacturing.
Under Automatic Route up to 49% and Government Route beyond 49%.
Investments from land-border countries are permanently barred.
ref: Proviso to Rule 6(a) of Foreign Exchange Management (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019
explanation: Under the proviso to Rule 6(a), an entity of a country which shares land border with India or where the beneficial owner of an investment into India is situated in or is a citizen of any such country, can invest only under the Government approval route. Automatic route is completely unavailable.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Overseas Direct Investment (ODI) Rules 2022 - Financial Commitment Limit
question: Under the Foreign Exchange Management (Overseas Investment) Rules, 2022, what is the maximum permissible limit of total financial commitment in all foreign entities by an Indian entity under the Automatic Route?
options: Up to 400% (four hundred percent) of the net worth of the Indian entity as per the last audited balance sheet, or USD 1 Billion per financial year, whichever is less.
Up to 100% of the net worth of the Indian entity.
Up to 200% of paid-up share capital exclusively.
Capped at USD 100 Million per project.
ref: Rule 13(1) and Schedule I of FEM (Overseas Investment) Rules, 2022
explanation: Under the Foreign Exchange Management (Overseas Investment) Rules, 2022, the total financial commitment made by an Indian entity in all foreign entities shall not exceed 400% of its net worth as per the last audited balance sheet, or as prescribed by RBI from time to time under the automatic route.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] External Commercial Borrowings (ECB) - Framework & Minimum Maturity
question: Under the Master Direction on External Commercial Borrowings (ECB) issued by the Reserve Bank of India, what is the Minimum Average Maturity Period (MAMP) for foreign currency denominated ECBs raised up to USD 750 Million per financial year under the Automatic Route for general corporate purposes?
options: Minimum Average Maturity Period (MAMP) of 5 years (or 3 years for eligible manufacturing sector companies).
MAMP of 1 year.
MAMP of 10 years without exception.
No maturity requirement if interest is paid semi-annually.
ref: RBI Master Direction No. 5/2018-19 on External Commercial Borrowings (ECB Framework)
explanation: Under the RBI ECB framework, the Minimum Average Maturity Period (MAMP) for general corporate / working capital purposes is 5 years. For specific manufacturing companies, it can be 3 years for borrowings up to USD 50 Million.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 13 - Penalties for Contravention of FEMA
question: If any person contravenes any provision of FEMA, 1999 or any rule, regulation, direction or order issued thereunder, what is the monetary penalty leviable under Section 13(1) where the amount involved is quantifiable?
options: Up to thrice (3 times) the sum involved in such contravention, and where the amount is not quantifiable, up to ₹2 Lakhs, and for continuing contravention a further penalty up to ₹5,000 per day.
Fixed penalty equal to 100% of the transaction amount.
Imprisonment for 7 years without option of monetary penalty.
A penalty up to ₹10 Lakhs strictly.
ref: Section 13(1) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
explanation: Under Section 13(1), if any person contravenes any provision of this Act, or any rule, regulation, notification, direction or order, he shall be liable to a penalty up to thrice the sum involved in such contravention where the amount is quantifiable, or up to two lakh rupees where the amount is not quantifiable, and where such contravention is a continuing one, further penalty which may extend to five thousand rupees for every day after the first day.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 15 - Compounding of Contraventions
question: Under Section 15 of FEMA, 1999 read with Foreign Exchange (Compounding Proceedings) Rules, 2000, which of the following contraventions CANNOT be compounded by the Reserve Bank of India?
options: A contravention where a similar contravention committed by the person was compounded within a period of three years from the date of the present contravention, or contraventions involving serious money laundering/hawala angles.
Failure to file Advance Reporting Form within 30 days of receiving inward remittance.
Delay in filing Form FC-GPR beyond 30 days of share allotment.
Borrowing ECB exceeding the prescribed all-in-cost ceiling.
ref: Section 15(1) proviso of FEMA, 1999 and Rule 4 of Compounding Proceedings Rules, 2000
explanation: Under the proviso to Section 15(1), where a contravention has been compounded, no further compounding of that contravention shall be done within a period of 3 years from the date on which that contravention was compounded. Any second contravention committed within 3 years must go to regular adjudication. Also, contraventions involving serious PMLA violations cannot be compounded by RBI.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 4 - Holding of Foreign Exchange by Resident Indian
question: Under Section 4 of FEMA, 1999 read with Foreign Exchange Management (Realisation, Repatriation and Surrender of Foreign Exchange) Regulations, 2015, what is the maximum amount of foreign currency notes/coins an individual resident in India can retain in cash for personal use?
options: Up to USD 2,000 (or its equivalent in foreign currency notes/coins) without opening an RFC(D) account.
Up to USD 10,000 in cash notes.
Zero cash retention; all foreign currency must be surrendered within 24 hours of landing in India.
Up to USD 50,000 provided it was received as a gift.
ref: Regulation 3 of FEM (Realisation, Repatriation and Surrender of Foreign Exchange) Regulations, 2015
explanation: Under Regulation 3 of FEM (Realisation, Repatriation and Surrender of Foreign Exchange) Regulations, a person resident in India is permitted to retain foreign currency notes, bank notes and foreign currency travellers' cheques exceeding not more than USD 2,000 or its equivalent in aggregate, provided they were acquired while on a visit abroad or from an authorized person for business travel.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 8 - Realisation and Repatriation of Foreign Exchange
question: An Indian exporter exports engineering goods worth USD 500,000 on January 1, 2024. Under Section 8 of FEMA read with Foreign Exchange Management (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations, within what period must the full export value of goods be realized and repatriated to India?
options: Within 9 months from the date of export (or 15 months if goods are exported to an overseas warehouse).
Within 30 days from the date of shipment.
Within 180 days without any power of extension.
Within 2 years as per international trade terms.
ref: Regulation 9 of FEM (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2016
explanation: Under Regulation 9, the amount representing the full value of goods, software or services exported shall be realised and repatriated to India within nine months from the date of export. For goods exported to an overseas warehouse, the period is 15 months from the date of shipment.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Acquisition of Immovable Property in India by PROI
question: Under the FEM (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019, can a Non-Resident Indian (NRI) or Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) acquire immovable property in India?
options: An NRI or OCI can acquire any immovable property in India other than agricultural land, farm house, or plantation property.
An NRI or OCI cannot acquire any property in India without prior approval of RBI.
An NRI can acquire agricultural land provided payment is made through NRE account.
An NRI can only lease property for a period not exceeding 3 years.
ref: Chapter IX read with Rule 24 of FEM (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019
explanation: Under Rule 24 of the Non-Debt Instruments Rules, an NRI or an OCI may acquire by way of purchase any immovable property in India other than agricultural land, farm house or plantation property, using funds received in India through normal banking channels by way of inward remittance or held in NRE/FCNR(B)/NRO account.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Acquisition of Immovable Property Outside India by PRII
question: Dr. Alok, a resident Indian doctor who was born and brought up in Delhi, wishes to purchase a residential flat in London for GBP 180,000. Under the Foreign Exchange Management (Overseas Investment) Rules, 2022, how can Dr. Alok legally acquire this property?
options: He can acquire the residential property outside India using the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) within the overall limit of USD 250,000 per financial year.
He must obtain prior special approval from the Union Cabinet.
A person resident in India is completely barred from acquiring any immovable property outside India.
He can acquire the property only by taking a loan from a London local bank without remitting any money from India.
ref: Rule 21 of Foreign Exchange Management (Overseas Investment) Rules, 2022
explanation: Under Rule 21(2) of the FEM (Overseas Investment) Rules, 2022, a person resident in India may acquire immovable property outside India by way of purchase out of the foreign exchange held in an RFC account or through remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) within the limit of USD 2,50,000 per financial year.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Authorised Person (AP) & Authorized Dealer Categories
question: Under Section 10 of FEMA, 1999, who empowers and issues licenses to Authorised Persons (including Authorized Dealers Category I, II, III and Full-Fledged Money Changers)?
options: The Reserve Bank of India, on an application made to it in this behalf, authorizes any person to deal in foreign exchange or in foreign securities as an authorized dealer, money changer or off-shore banking unit.
The Securities and Exchange Board of India.
The Ministry of External Affairs in consultation with Ministry of Finance.
The Indian Banks' Association (IBA).
ref: Section 10(1) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
explanation: Under Section 10(1), the Reserve Bank may, on an application made to it in this behalf, authorize any person to be known as an authorized person to deal in foreign exchange or in foreign securities, as an authorized dealer, money changer or off-shore banking unit or in any other manner as it deems fit.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Export of Services & Softex Form Requirement
question: An IT services company in Bengaluru exports software code to a client in Germany via internet data transmission. What statutory compliance must the company perform under FEMA regulations?
options: File a SOFTEX form in triplicate with the designated STPI (Software Technology Parks of India) within 30 days from the date of invoice/certification.
File an EDF (Export Declaration Form) with the Commissioner of Customs.
Software exports via internet are exempt from all filings under FEMA.
Obtain an import-export license from the local municipal corporation.
ref: Regulation 6 of FEM (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2016
explanation: Under Regulation 6(1) of FEM (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations, every exporter of software in physical or non-physical (satellite/internet) form shall submit a declaration in Form SOFTEX to the designated official of STPI or SEZ within 30 days of the date of invoice for certification.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Non-Resident Bank Accounts (NRE vs NRO vs FCNR(B))
question: Which of the following statements regarding Non-Resident External (NRE) accounts and Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) accounts is ACCURATE under FEMA regulations?
options: NRE accounts are repatriable without limit and interest earned is exempt from Indian income-tax, whereas NRO accounts have a repatriation ceiling of USD 1 Million per financial year and interest is taxable.
NRO accounts allow unlimited tax-free repatriation while NRE accounts are completely non-repatriable.
Both NRE and NRO accounts can only be maintained in US Dollars.
NRE accounts can be credited with legitimate rupee earnings originating from within India without restriction.
ref: Schedule 1 and Schedule 3 of FEM (Deposit) Regulations, 2016
explanation: Under FEM (Deposit) Regulations, 2016: NRE accounts are maintained in Indian Rupees, principal and interest are freely repatriable without limit, and interest is exempt from income tax u/s 10(4)(ii). NRO accounts are maintained for domestic earnings; funds can be repatriated up to USD 1 Million per financial year upon payment of applicable taxes.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 37 - Directorate of Enforcement (ED) Powers
question: Under Section 37 of FEMA, 1999, who exercises powers of investigation in respect of contraventions under the Act?
options: The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) officers, who exercise powers conferred on Income-tax authorities under the Income-tax Act, 1961 with respect to search, seizure, summons and inspection.
The local State Police Station under the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The Central Vigilance Commission exclusively.
The Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) under Companies Act.
ref: Section 37(1) and 37(3) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
explanation: Under Section 37(1), the Director of Enforcement and other officers of Enforcement shall take up for investigation the contravention referred to in section 13. Under Section 37(3), the officers of the Directorate of Enforcement shall exercise the like powers which are conferred on income-tax authorities under the Income-tax Act, 1961.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 3 - Dealing in Foreign Exchange Prohibition
question: Under Section 3 of FEMA, 1999, save as otherwise provided in this Act, rules or regulations, no person shall:
options: Deal in or transfer any foreign exchange or foreign security to any person not being an authorized person, or make any payment to or for credit of any person resident outside India in any manner.
Maintain a passport issued by the Government of India.
Buy goods manufactured outside India from a local supermarket.
Exchange currency at an authorized airport foreign exchange counter.
ref: Section 3(a) and 3(b) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
explanation: Under Section 3, save as otherwise provided in this Act, rules or regulations, no person shall: (a) deal in or transfer any foreign exchange or foreign security to any person not being an authorized person; (b) make any payment to or for the credit of any person resident outside India in any manner; (c) receive payments on behalf of PROI without general/special permission of RBI.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 19 - Appeal to High Court under FEMA
question: Any person aggrieved by any decision or order of the Appellate Tribunal for Foreign Exchange may file an appeal to the High Court under Section 35 within what period, and on what grounds?
options: Within 60 days from the date of communication of the decision/order, on any question of law arising out of such order (extendable by High Court for a further period not exceeding 60 days).
Within 30 days on question of fact or law.
Within 90 days directly to the Supreme Court.
No appeal lies against the orders of the Appellate Tribunal under FEMA.
ref: Section 35 of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
explanation: Under Section 35, any person aggrieved by any decision or order of the Appellate Tribunal may file an appeal to the High Court within 60 days from the date of communication of the decision or order on any question of law arising out of such order. The High Court may condone delay for a further period not exceeding sixty days.
